definition: Information that describes other data, revealing details about when, where, how, and by whom content was created, modified, or accessed without showing the actual content itself.
metaDescription: Learn about metadata - the hidden information in your files and communications that can reveal sensitive details about your activities and privacy.
simpleExplanation: Metadata is like invisible labels attached to your digital files and activities. While you see a photo or email, metadata contains hidden details like when it was taken, what device was used, or your location when you created it.
whyItMatters: Metadata can expose sensitive information about your habits, relationships, and movements even when the actual content is protected. Companies and governments often analyze metadata to build detailed profiles of individuals.
technicalDetail: Metadata is structured information embedded in files, network packets, and system logs. Common types include EXIF data in images (camera settings, GPS coordinates, timestamps), email headers (routing information, client details), and file system metadata (creation dates, access times, user permissions). This data persists even when files are shared or transmitted.

examples.explanation: A photo you share online might contain GPS coordinates showing exactly where it was taken, the camera model used, and the exact time and date, even if you think you're only sharing the image.
Every email contains hidden headers showing the sender's IP address, email client, routing servers, and timestamps that can reveal location and communication patterns.
A Word document might contain the author's name, company information, edit history, and comments from previous versions that you thought were deleted.
